clue.text: See 10
Short hold-up stops motorists from greeting

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the last letter off the word hold
in a down clue, up means the shortened word is read from the bottom to the top
the reversed fragment plugs the gap between the motorists' letters, as a cork stops a bottle

blocks.note: the AA is Britain's Automobile Association, the motoring organisation
hold is taken as written before being cut and turned

explanation.surface: A brief traffic jam keeps drivers from saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' reads as a single noun meaning delay, but it splits into hold plus the direction up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used both as hello and goodbye, so it is a salutation.

clue.text: Alternatives to back and forth?

blocks.note: in racing you can back a horse to win, or bet on it both to win and to be placed
back and forth suggests motion in both directions, that is, going either way

explanation.walkthrough: An each-way bet in British racing is two bets in one: the horse to win, and the horse to be placed in the first few. The question mark flags the punning reading of 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a two-part wager offering alternatives, and also means in both directions, which back and forth describes.

clue.text: Group of seals across river having black look for no mongrel

indicators.note: the pod stretches across the other letters, with its first letter on one side and the rest on the other

blocks.note: a pod is the collective noun for a group of seals or whales
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A gang of seals crossing a river glares at a passing dog, which is no mongrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a North Yorkshire river much used by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pure-blood animal has unmixed ancestry, the opposite of a mongrel of mixed breeding.

clue.text: Sums up for a tax of nothing?

blocks.note: per means for each or for a, as in per annum
O looks like zero, nothing
rates were the British local property tax

explanation.surface: Someone totting up the figures for a tax that charges nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the tax British councils levied on property before the council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To perorate is to deliver the concluding summary of a speech, so the verb means summarises at the end.

clue.text: Look too and fro?

indicators.note: a play on to and fro: the word runs the same in either direction, so it reads one way and back again

blocks.note: a verb meaning to consult or look in a source, as when you check a dictionary

explanation.surface: A glance cast this way and that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' is the setter's pun on 'to'; the whole clue defines a word for consulting that reads the same back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to a book is to consult or look in it, and the word reads identically in either direction.

clue.text: She'll help to get froth on top

definitions.text: She'll help to get froth on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second, so it is placed on top

blocks.note: barm is the yeasty froth that forms on fermenting beer
aid is a straight synonym for help

explanation.surface: A woman behind the bar who knows how to pour a pint with a good head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pub worker pulls pints with a frothy top, while the wordplay stacks the froth over the help.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman serving drinks in a pub helps produce the head of foam on each glass of beer she pours.

clue.text: See 10 across
They never got off the ground when holding South American's seat

indicators.note: the extinct birds grip the abbreviations between their letters

blocks.clueFragment: They never got off the ground
blocks.note: dodos were flightless birds, so they never flew
S is the compass abbreviation
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Grounded aircraft and a Latin American's chair, an odd pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They never got off the ground' suggests failed aircraft or projects, but it is the flightless dodos.
explanation.definitionFit: A dos-a-dos is a sofa or carriage seat on which two people sit back to back.

clue.text: Jack binds books in covering

indicators.note: the male wraps round the books like a binding

blocks.note: a jack is the male of certain animals, such as the donkey
NT, the New Testament, is a crossword's usual books

explanation.surface: A man wrapping volumes in a protective jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; here it means a male animal, as in jackass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak, and by extension any layer that covers something, like a mantle of snow.

clue.text: Crazy American fliers at war cannot plead fear of enemy fire or madness. It won't wash. There's a no-good catch to define sane.

annotation.answer: A CONCERN FOR ONES FAC EOWNSA FE TYT HATW ER EREALAN DOFD ANGE RSPR OCE SSOFARATI ONA LMI NDINTHE IM M EDIATEWA STHE

definitions.text: Crazy American fliers at war cannot plead fear of enemy fire or madness. It won't wash. There's a no-good catch to define sane.

indicators.note: crazy means wildly disordered, so the rest of the clue's letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.clueFragment: American fliers at war cannot plead fear of enemy fire or madness. It won't wash. There's a no-good catch to define sane.
blocks.note: every letter after the first word is used exactly once

explanation.surface: A summary of Joseph Heller's novel: US airmen cannot get grounded by pleading insanity, because fearing death proves they are sane.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the line from Catch-22 that states the catch, and the clue both rearranges into it and describes it. The quotation runs through the linked lights in the order 10, 7 down, 22, 1, 14 down, 11, 23, 15, 20.
explanation.definitionFit: Heller's novel defines Catch-22 with this sentence: worrying about real danger proves sanity, so no airman can be excused flying as mad.

clue.text: See 10
10 doesn't start off keen to have small part put in code

indicators.note: the number loses its opening letter, the one it starts off with

blocks.note: the number is spelt out as a word
to keen is to wail or cry in mourning
PT is the abbreviation of part, a short form

explanation.surface: An eager agent tucks a short fragment into a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to the long quotation at 10 across, but it is just the number ten. 'Keen' is the verb meaning to lament, not the adjective eager.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt a message is to convert it into a cipher so outsiders cannot read it.

clue.text: 2 mice suffering from bile in blood

indicators.note: the letters are in distress and twisted out of shape

blocks.note: the answer to 2 down, a Hawaiian greeting, supplies five letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two lab mice ill with a liver complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' reads as the number two but points to the answer at 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholaemia is the medical term for the presence of bile pigments circulating in the bloodstream.

clue.text: Double Dutch is part of one's small eccentricity

indicators.note: the doubled letter becomes part of the word by sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
two Ds, D being the abbreviation for Dutch
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Gibberish is part and parcel of one's little quirks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Dutch' is British slang for gibberish, but here it is two Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddness is the quality of being strange or peculiar, which is what eccentricity describes.

clue.text: See 10 across
See 10
Science of sound developed on chips

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Phonics is an old name for acoustics, the study of sound, before it came to mean a reading method.

clue.text: Holyfield is also on record as the holder

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: ever as in the best ever, the best on record
and is a synonym for also

explanation.surface: Holyfield is also in the record books as champion, the title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holder' suggests a boxing title holder; it signals containment. Evander Holyfield is an American world heavyweight boxing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Evander is the first name of the boxer Holyfield, so it stands for the man.

clue.text: Rotten in the '70s, roughly speaking

indicators.note: the answer is spoken approximately like a word for a ten-year period

blocks.note: the 1970s were a decade

explanation.surface: A sneer at how bad things were in the nineteen-seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed food or wood has gone bad through decomposition, so it is putrid.

clue.text: Old king has to get behind in artwork

indicators.note: the delay is placed in the middle of the king's name

blocks.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
to lag is to fall behind

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch falling behind with a picture he commissioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it describes any old king, but Old King Cole is one name from the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is a picture made by gluing scraps of paper and other materials, a kind of art.

clue.text: A fair vehicle

blocks.note: reads as a just or reasonable thing, but means a travelling funfair
a small electric car that riders bump into one another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as honest or just; it is the funfair, where these cars are a classic ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a bumper car, a ride at a funfair, so it is literally a car at a fair.

clue.text: See 10
One old alphabet that was drawn up to bug adult

indicators.note: in a down answer, drawing it up means reading it from the bottom upward

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ogam, or ogham, is an ancient Irish alphabet of strokes

explanation.surface: An archaic script once compiled to annoy a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like the verb annoy, but it is the noun insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, mature stage of an insect after metamorphosis, so it is a grown insect.

clue.text: See 10 across
See 10
Mayday, including previous month, getting too unsettled for gypsophila and its ilk

indicators.note: the distress call holds the other letters within it
the three letters are disturbed and rearranged

blocks.note: SOS is the other standard distress signal
April, abbreviated, comes just before May
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A May Day emergency call involving April and some disturbed flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previous month' works because the clue starts with May: the month before is April.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaproot is a name for gypsophila species whose roots yield a soapy lather, so the plural covers it and its relatives.

clue.text: 14 is not part of the answer

definitions.text: 14 is not part of the answer

blocks.note: 14 across means strangeness, literally the quality of being odd, and that is the opposite of being divisible by two
only the adjective inside the abstract noun goes in the grid, a piece of the longer word

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's nod to odd and even: the 14 across answer is the quality of being odd, which is just what this answer's noun form is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and even are the paired opposites for whole numbers, so the word that oddness is not supplies its counterpart.
